questions.question_text:
Water flows into a container at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=8t+3$ litres per second, and the container holds $7$ litres when $t=0$.
Find $V$ as a function of $t$.

options.why: Integrated $8t$ as $8t^{2}$, forgetting to divide by the new index $2$.
Integrated correctly but left out the initial volume, taking $C=0$.
Integrated $8t$ as $8t^{2}$ and also left out the initial volume.

questions.question_text:
A stockpile changes at $\dfrac{dW}{dt}=4t+1$ kilograms per day.
Find the total change in $W$ between $t=2$ and $t=5$ days.

options.why: Substituted only the upper limit $t=5$ and never subtracted the value at $t=2$.
Integrated $4t$ as $4t^{2}$ instead of $2t^{2}$, then subtracted correctly.
Integrated $4t$ as $4t^{2}$ and also used the upper limit only.

questions.question_text:
A tank holds $25$ litres at $t=0$, and water flows in at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=6t-4$ litres per minute.
How much water is in the tank after $5$ minutes?

options.why: Omitted the initial value: this is the change in volume, not the amount in the tank.
Integrated $6t$ as $6t^{2}$ instead of $3t^{2}$, and also omitted the initial $25$ litres.
Integrated $6t$ as $6t^{2}$ instead of $3t^{2}$ before adding the initial $25$ litres.

questions.question_text:
A tank holds $36$ litres at $t=0$, and water flows in at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=2t$ litres per minute.
Find the time at which the tank holds $100$ litres.

options.why: Omitted the initial $36$ litres and solved $t^{2}=100$ instead of $t^{2}+36=100$.
Set the rate equal to the amount, solving $2t=100$ instead of building $V(t)$ first.
Took the square root of the initial value $36$ rather than solving for $t$.

questions.question_text:
A quantity of fuel changes at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=2t-14$ litres per hour.
Find the total change in the volume of fuel between $t=0$ and $t=4$ hours.

options.why: Found the right size but ignored the negative value of the integral.
Integrated $2t$ as $2t^{2}$ instead of $t^{2}$.
Integrated $2t$ as $2t^{2}$ and also ignored the negative value of the integral.

questions.solution_text:
$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{4}(2t-14)\,dt$
$=\left[t^{2}-14t\right]_{0}^{4}$
$=16-56$
$=-40\text{ L}$
The integral is negative, so the volume decreases by $40$ litres.

questions.question_text:

When $t=0$, $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=10$ litres per minute and $Q=3$ litres.
Find $Q$ when $t=2$ minutes.

options.why: Omitted the initial amount $Q=3$ at the second integration.
Omitted the initial rate of $10$, so the $10t$ term never appeared in $Q$.
Omitted both initial conditions, taking each constant of integration as zero.

questions.question_text:
A gas expands at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=12e^{0.5t}$ cubic centimetres per second, and $V=4\text{ cm}^{3}$ when $t=0$.
Find $V$ as a function of $t$.

options.why: Wrote the initial value straight in as $C$ instead of solving $24e^{0}+C=4$.
Multiplied by $0.5$ instead of dividing by it when integrating $e^{0.5t}$.
Multiplied by $0.5$ instead of dividing, and wrote the initial value straight in as $C$.
